enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **a)** Write a story which ends with "...that is why I can never have confidence in anybody again"
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: my close friend Ngu and the secret I trusted him with.
2. Build-up: a school fees problem, my plan to sell a small piece of land left by my late father, and my confession to him.
3. Climax: the secret is told to my uncle, who takes the land.
4. Consequences: the loss, my shame, Ngu's excuses.
5. Ending with the required sentence.

**Model composition (483 words)**

Ngu and I had been friends since our first day in Form One. We shared our books, our lunch and, above all, our secrets. People in our quarter called us "the twins", and I truly believed that I could trust him with my life.

In my fifth year, my father died suddenly, and my mother was left to feed three children on the small income she earned from selling vegetables. One evening, she told me with tears in her eyes that she could not pay my school fees any longer. I walked out of the house heavily, and my feet carried me to Ngu's compound. There, under the mango tree, I told him everything. I also confided in him a secret plan. My father had left me a small piece of land behind our house, and I had decided to sell it quietly so that I could pay my fees and my brothers' fees without telling my uncle, who always wanted to control our family affairs.

Ngu listened carefully, patted my shoulder and promised, "Your secret is safe with me. I will never say a word." I went home with a light heart, certain that a true friend had given me strength.

Three days later, I was called to my uncle's house. When I entered the sitting room, he was seated on his large chair, his eyes red with anger, and my mother was standing in a corner, trembling. "So you want to sell your father's land behind my back?" he shouted. "Who do you think you are?" My heart almost stopped. Only one person on earth knew about that plan.

I learnt later that Ngu had gone to my uncle the very next morning. My uncle had promised him a bag of rice and some money in exchange for any information about our family land. My friend had sold my trust for a few coins. With the support of the elders, my uncle took the land and sold it for himself, and my mother and I were left with nothing but pain.

I stayed at home for two weeks, ashamed to see anybody. When Ngu came to the house, he stood at the door and tried to explain. "I only wanted to help the family," he said, looking at the ground. I did not answer. I simply closed the door in his face. Months passed, and I finally found a small job in a bookshop, where I worked in the evenings and earned enough to return to school. The fees were paid at last, but something inside me had broken.

Since that sad experience, I smile at everybody, but I keep my thoughts to myself. I have learnt that a person who has been betrayed by the friend he loved most finds it very hard to open his heart again, and that is why I can never have confidence in anybody again.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. The story does not end with the exact sentence given, or the ending is not prepared by the events.
2. A list of events without build-up, climax and consequences.
